audit.whatIsWrong: Lane difficulty text treats levels 4-5 as Mundo's window because 'his Heart Zapper W uptime increases', without saying what Heart Zapper actually does or how to beat it.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s with a 325 range. It stores a portion of the damage Mundo takes and only heals him if the recast burst hits an enemy. Rumble can simply leave the 325 radius before the recast and deny the entire heal — that is the mechanical answer the difficulty section was missing.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 are Mundo's window only if you stand in Heart Zapper's 325 range for the recast; step out and he keeps the damage taken with no heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ items spike says Maximum Dosage lets Mundo 'survive almost any trade' and pairs it with Warmog's regen, but never gives the cooldown or what the heal scales from.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s cooldown at all ranks and heals a percent of MISSING health, then regenerates over time. Flat 120s means the post-R window is a hard, trackable spike for Rumble, and 'missing health' means poking him to low actually increases the heal — the opposite of what the current text implies.
audit.corrected: Maximum Dosage is flat 120s and heals off missing health; the trackable spike is the two minutes after he uses it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two ability facts are wrong. (a) Infected Bonesaw is described as 'percent-HP magic damage' poke; Riot's text says it damages based on the target's CURRENT health. (b) The late-game text says Maximum Dosage 'heals an enormous percentage of his max HP'; it heals a percent of MISSING health.
audit.why: Current-health scaling means the bonesaw is strongest when Rumble is full and tapers as Rumble drops, so it softens but cannot finish — that changes when you respect it. Missing-health scaling on R means chip-poking him low before he ults feeds the heal. Both errors point the player the wrong way.
audit.corrected: Infected Bonesaw scales off your current health (hits hardest at full, tapers as you drop, 975 range, 4s flat cooldown). Maximum Dosage heals a percent of his missing health. Heart Zapper heals only if the recast burst hits — leave 325 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldowns block names Heart Zapper but gives no numbers and no second entry.
audit.why: Real numbers make the advice actionable: Heart Zapper 15-17s, Blunt Force Trauma 9 down to 6s, Infected Bonesaw a flat 4s, Maximum Dosage flat 120s.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block now carries Heart Zapper's 15-17s and Maximum Dosage's flat 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions that Rumble has no immobilising effect, so Mundo's Goes Where He Pleases passive never gets popped in this lane.
audit.why: Rumble's only CC is a slow (Electro Harpoon, The Equalizer). Neither is an immobilise, so Mundo's cannister passive stays banked for the jungler's CC. Left out of the edits because the useful phrasing would be a non-interaction, but recorded here.

edits.after: Step out of Heart Zapper's 325 range before it recasts — no burst hit, no heal
edits.before: Use Electro-Harpoon double-slow to shut down his Q cleaver from being thrown freely

edits.after: At Level 1 you have a real Flamespitter advantage — Infected Bonesaw threatens from 975 but needs aim, while your Q cone only needs him to walk up for CS. Stand at max Flamespitter range and deny his farm with chip damage, but respect the bonesaw angle: it scales off your CURRENT health, so it hits hardest while you are full and tapers as you drop. It softens you, it does not finish you. By Level 2 you can double Electro Harpoon him off a Flamespitter tick, and the MR shred stacks, so the second harpoon and the Q behind it both bite harder. At Level 3 you have your full kit, but his passive regen starts mattering — you will not poke him to a kill without anti-heal already bought or Ignite behind it. You are ahead on damage output, not on kill threat.
edits.before: At Level 1 you have a real Flamespitter advantage — his percent-HP poke (Q cleaver) is threatening but requires aim, while your Q cone just needs him to walk up for CS. Stand at max Flamespitter range and deny his farm with chip damage, but respect his cleaver angle; it deals percent-HP magic damage and will set you behind if it lands freely. By Level 2 you can double-E-harpoon him after a Flamespitter tick to burn out his regen window between trades. At Level 3 you have your full kit, but Mundo's passive regen starts mattering — you will not be able to poke him to a kill without anti-heal already in your inventory or backed up by ignite. Accept that you are ahead in damage output but not in kill threat yet.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are deceptively his window, not yours. Heart Zapper is a 17-down-to-15 second cooldown that banks a portion of every point of damage you put into him and pays it back as healing on the recast burst — but only if that burst actually hits someone. So the answer is mechanical: when he pops W, stop feeding it and walk outside its 325 range before the recast, and he eats the damage with none of the heal. Flamespitter stays the right tool; max-health magic damage is not something he itemises around. Do not Overheat chasing him — a silence while he holds the HP lead is a death sentence. At Level 6 the lane tilts back: The Equalizer zones him off his own CS, and a wall laid across his path makes him walk through the burn and slow to reach you.
edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are deceptively his window, not yours. His Heart Zapper W is up more often, his HP pool is massive, and his regen between trades outpaces your poke unless you have Oblivion Orb or an ignite ticking. Flamespitter is still the right tool — it deals percent-HP magic damage and he cannot ignore it — but respect that every time you back off to reset Heat, his W restores a chunk of what you burned. Do not Overheat chasing him; a silence while he has the HP lead is a death sentence. At Level 6 the lane flips in your favor: Equalizer lets you zone him off his own CS, drop a wall across his path to force him through damage and slow, and the threat of it alone stops him from simply walking forward into you freely.

edits.after: At two items Mundo is close to unkillable in a straight lane fight. Maximum Dosage heals a percent of his MISSING health and then regenerates over a long duration, so chipping him to 30% before he ults only makes the heal bigger — burst him from full or not at all, and keep anti-heal running. It is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, so the two minutes after he presses it are your real window. Your value is no longer this lane; it is firing The Equalizer into 5v5s where his bulk stops mattering and his team cannot sidestep a map-wide burning wall. Rotate, split-threaten to force his team to answer, and save the ult for objectives where his frontline walk becomes a liability.
edits.before: At two items Mundo becomes nearly unkillable in a straight lane fight. Maximum Dosage R heals an enormous percentage of his max HP, Warmog's regen ticks between every trade, and he starts tanking your Flamespitter without flinching. Do not try to 1v1 him unless he has burned his R and you have anti-heal running. Your value is no longer in winning this lane — it is in firing Equalizer into 5v5 fights where his bulk becomes irrelevant and his team cannot dodge a map-wide burning wall. Stay relevant by rotating, split-threatening to force his team to react, and saving Equalizer for objectives where his frontline walk becomes a liability.

notes: Rumble has no immobilising effect (Electro Harpoon and The Equalizer are slows only), so Dr. Mundo's Goes Where He Pleases cannister passive is never popped by Rumble in lane — it stays banked against your jungler's CC. Not written into the page because the phrasing would be a non-interaction. Kit-flag misfires on rumble.json: Scrap Shield (W) carries 'knockup' and 'terrain' flags, but Riot's description is a shield plus a move-speed burst with no displacement and no terrain; The Equalizer's 'terrain' flag is likewise a damage/slow line, not a wall that blocks pathing. The _missing-interactions entry claiming Mundo 'bypasses stacking resistances (Maximum Dosage R)' is a misfire — R is a heal. The genuine resistance-bypass is Infected Bonesaw's current-health damage. The _missing-interactions 'autoreset' claim for Blunt Force Trauma is not supported by Riot's text and was not asserted.
